question: Calculate the gravitational force between two masses of 5 kg each placed 2 m apart.
gold_answer:
# Solved Numerical

---

## Gravitational Field Problem

### Problem
Calculate the gravitational force between two identical masses of $5 \text{ kg}$ each placed at a center-to-center distance of $2 \text{ m}$ apart.

### Given
* First mass ($m_1$) = $5 \text{ kg}$
* Second mass ($m_2$) = $5 \text{ kg}$
* Distance apart ($r$) = $2 \text{ m}$
* Gravitational Constant ($G$) = $6.67 \times 10^{-11} \text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{kg}^2$

### Formula
$$F = G \frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2}$$

### Substitution
$$F = (6.67 \times 10^{-11}) \times \frac{5 \times 5}{2^2}$$

### Calculation
$$F = (6.67 \times 10^{-11}) \times \frac{25}{4}$$

$$F = (6.67 \times 10^{-11}) \times 6.25$$

$$F = 4.16875 \times 10^{-10} \text{ N}$$

### Final Answer
**Gravitational Force ($F$) = $4.17 \times 10^{-10} \text{ N}$**

### Interpretation
This reflects an incredibly weak mutual attraction force, demonstrating why gravity is imperceptible between everyday objects and only becomes significant with planetary-scale masses.
